blocks.text: Deck innovations

First and foremost, this half-deck has a special deck with Exalted wizards: more powerful versions of the unique wizards present in the normal deck. Keep the special deck next to the market. How it works: after you have promoted one of the unique wizards, in the same turn or at any time afterwards, you can look for that wizard’s Exalted version in the special deck, and recruit them by paying the printed cost. Think of it as investing the time and resources for your wizard to study and become more powerful to work for you — now that’s what I call a job promotion! Henceforth, that Exalted wizard will sit face-up on your play area and function as a continuous sixth card for you. Each player may have only one Exalted wizard. One could even make the Exalted wizards as tiles instead of cards.

Secondly, every card on this deck also has a “secondary aspect”, which is an arcane school. They activate Arcane Focus effects, kind of like in the Elemental deck, but these powers are slightly stronger because there are fewer cards for each school. However, there are 8 cards in the market deck that can activate any Arcane Focus.
Finally, card #25 (Acererak the Exalted Devourer) can devour troops: send them to the devoured area.
Cards v.1.1
Sorted by Aspect:
Obedience Cards
1) Prodigious Novice Arcanist: They can activate any Arcane Focus, but only once per turn. Think of them helping the other wizards cast their spells.

2) Enduring Spellbook: an alluring artifact to any wizard. The discount also works for recruiting Exalted wizards from the special deck. Or you can keep it in your deck to facilitate Arcane Focuses and cash in some VP while you’re at it.
Ambition Cards
3) Enchanter: enchant an enemy troop to leave its post or send it somewhere else. Also, its Focus lets you promote any card you played this turn, including itself.
4) Necromancer: why keep the devoured cards out of the game?

11) Ezzat: every turn you get the chance to clean your deck and pollute an opponent’s. I ran out of room on the card, but just to be clear: the card promoted face down will score negative inner-circle VP.
12) Tasha the Witch: she dealt with powerful fiends from the Abyss, and they loved a sacrifice in their honor.
19) Ezzat the Exalted Usurper: a bit of a shot in the dark?

20) Tasha the Exalted Witch Queen: Being a powerful conjurer, Tasha can easily open portals and force enemies through. Or she can make more sacrifices to fortify fiendish friendships. About the effect: when you activate her, you take any card from the market, play it as your own once, and then promote it straight into your inner circle.
Conquest Cards
5) Abjurer: banish the enemies away. Also, you may manage to secure your position. You can put a point token on one of your troops just to remind everyone of that effect.
9) Conjurer: literally teleport enemies or allies.
13) Halaster: paranoid, crazy, powerful mage. Very destructive.
14) Trobriand: more bonuses for keeping area control.
21) Halaster the Exalted Mad Mage: more (seemingly) mindless destruction.
22) Trobriand the Exalted Metal Mage: huge focus on the area control aspect.
Guile Cards

7) Diviner: planning is usually a lot easier when you can see the future... And messing with an opponent’s plans is nice as well. Also, because this is a game of intrigue and conflict, I think this card will work best if the player tells the other opponents what cards he saw, though of course that is not mandatory.
8) Illusionist: agents disguised to infiltrate, gather intel and sabotage. You can even do both on the same turn if Illusion Focus activates!
15) Mordenkainen: possibly sweeten your options for this turn.
16) Vizeran DeVir: a simpler card, among all the crazy wizards. An austere drow.
23) Mordenkainen the Exalted Planewalker: since there rarely are cards costing 2 or less, whatever comes will be a great deal.
24) Vizeran DeVir the Exalted Archmage: how about an exchange they literally can’t deny? When you take the opponent’s card, bring it into your discard pile.
Malice Cards
9) Transmuter: simple, but thus versatile.
10) Evoker: A good card for early and mid-game, but its Focus works all the way.
17) Acererak: he can cast a Resurrection spell. Surely the resurrected creature will want to work for your house after such a favor.
18) Muiral: as a good transmuter, he can bolster his allies.
25) Acererak the Exalted Devourer: after he has killed the troops, he now consumes every speck of energy they might still have in order to feed his insatiable hunger… and you gain 2 extra VP for it!

26) Muiral the Exalted Misshapen: this dude got his kicks from hunting adventurers, so you send your weaker allies as bait. You devour X cards from your hand to devour X cards from the opponents’ decks.

Suggestions
A few changes may work well in getting the deck to show what it was designed to do.

Katunik’s first suggestion was to replace one of the initial Nobles for a Prodigious Novice Arcanist. If there are fewer than 4 players, the remaining Arcanists go into the market deck, as per the normal game.

Then, I thought about giving a secret random unique wizard to each player as the first card in their discard pile, so they could start planning purchases from round one (considering your table does not forbid perusing your own discard pile). Though this initial asymmetry may be displeasing to some players, I think it could be worth a try.

Also, about the Exalted wizards, I thought of a few options for how they could work (I had the first option in mind when I wrote their effects, after all it is a race to get more powerful assets to fight for your house):
• The Exalted wizard is a sixth card you can play every turn, or;
• It is a sixth card option, but you can still play only five cards on your turn (maybe it will be a little more balanced, yet still powerful?), and also;
• Players can have more than one Exalted Wizard in their house, but can only activate one per turn (activating more than one would surely snowball too fast).
SHADOWS OF THE GREAT WYRM
Faction Profile: The Jaezred Chaulssin
"The Matrons think they weave the web. They fail to realize that shadows are cast by much larger wings." — Mauzzkyl Jaezred

blocks.text: The Jaezred Chaulssin is a shadow-whisper in the dark—a clandestine council of shadow-dragon-blooded drow, known as the Zekyl, and their ancient Shadow Dragon progenitors. They have looked upon the spider-matriarchy of Lolth and found it wanting, choosing instead the path of calculated subversion and the cold logic of the void.

blocks.text: Tyrants of the Underdark: The Delver’s Company

runs.text: Tyrants of the Underdark: The Delver’s Company

blocks.text: Expansion Overview: The Delver’s Company is a high-stakes half-deck expansion that introduces a parallel economy. Players must balance territorial conquest with the management of their Hoard—a collection of powerful but volatile equipment and artifacts. With a d20-based Skill Check system, fortune can shift in an instant, rewarding the bold and punishing the unprepared.

Activation Cost: When you activate a Treasure's ability, you resolve the effect and then discard the Treasure to the Treasure discard pile.
